chapter_title: Concerning the Three Creations of the Flesh: the ones that were brought forth [...]; and the ones that were begotten by the Abortions; and the ones that were formed of themselves.
chapter_note: This chapter is almost entirely oldest teaching layer — a systematic cosmological classification of plant life according to the type of cosmic ruler whose 'thought' produced them. The mapping is consistently cosmos→cosmos: ruler types (flesh-eating, grass-eating, mixed) → plant categories (nourishing trees, bitter trees, neutral trees). Despite heavy lacunae, the teaching structure is clearly preserved. The only non-substrate material is the single-line dialogue frame opening. No editorial bridge, institutional, or exhortation material is present. The zero substrate register score reflects the pipeline's narrow marker vocabulary (zoomorphic/metal/taste), not the actual content, which is unmistakably substrate teaching about cosmic process → natural taxonomy.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic attribution with no cosmological content. 'Once again our enlightener speaks to his disciples' — standard dialogue frame marker.

paragraphs.core_text: All these animals that you see, and also the rest of the [crea]tures [...] of the earth, confirm them in three likeness[es ...]: some from [...] abortions. Others, however, form their own selves in their shape [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Three-fold cosmological classification of creatures: brought forth, begotten by abortions, self-formed. This is the chapter's core taxonomic structure. Heavily lacunose but the systematic three-fold enumeration is characteristic of the oldest teaching layer. 'You see' is pedagogical address within the teaching tradition, not editorial framing.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, their nourishment is thre[e ...] light in them, if they shall wish [...]. [...] they eat see[ds and] fr[uit ...]; they eat seeds and fruit. The [...] it entirely, and they [...] the three archetyp[es] from their nature and the [...] the time when they are on the ea[rth ...]; they are seized [...] in their [...]. The Ambassador [...] all powers [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Three-fold nourishment classification paralleling the three-fold creature classification. 'Three archetypes from their nature' is systematic cosmological teaching. The Ambassador (cosmic figure) and powers are elements of the cosmic narrative. Extremely fragmentary but the structure is clearly substrate: cosmic agents → natural processes.

paragraphs.core_text: [N] it [...], first [...]. ⟨p.247⟩ Plant them generally to this name: shoots and grass. It formed the bad, bitter trees, the reeds and the thorns and the [...] and these others that are like them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Plant taxonomy within the cosmic classification system. 'Bad, bitter trees, reeds, thorns' are natural categories produced by the cosmic process. Both sides of the mapping stay within the system: cosmic formation process → plant types. The impersonal 'it formed' is characteristic substrate voice.

paragraphs.core_text: For that thought belongs to the flesh-eating rulers. Still, these [that were] planted (belong to) grass and gourds, since they are in their essence. Nevertheless, [this t]ho[ugh]t that came down from the rulers, as they are in fruit and grass first and shall not be planted in flesh and blood, it formed the trees that shall give nourishing fru[it], as their gourds are sweet.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological-correspondential mapping: ruler type (flesh-eating) → their 'thought' → the type of plant produced. The 'thought' (ennoia) is the cosmic driving force of reproduction. Both sides internal to the cosmic system. The logic is systematic: the nature of the ruler determines the nature of the plant. 'Sweet gourds' and 'nourishing fruit' are correspondential qualities mapped to the cosmic origin.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this thou[ght] that came down from the powers that eat m[ea]t and also eat grass and gourds, it has formed the trees that shall not produce any nourishment. Their fruits belong neither to good nor evil.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the three-fold classification: powers that eat both meat and vegetation → trees with neutral, non-nourishing fruit. The 'neither good nor evil' quality corresponds to the mixed nature of the ruler type. 'Again' marks systematic enumeration continuation, not editorial bridge. Both sides remain within the cosmic taxonomy.
